## Critique
- claim-1: Correct. Inclusion of the smaller rectangle in the larger rectangle reverses inclusion of the corresponding Schur-basis complements, proving the ideal inclusion. The argument actually holds for all \(p,c\ge1\).
- claim-2: Correct. The quotient map retains precisely the interval basis elements lying in the smaller box and kills the others, so its restriction is surjective. Its \(\Lambda\)-linearity and that surjectivity give the stated equality of positive-degree submodules and hence the surjection on indecomposable quotients.

## Required revisions
- None. Under the stated Schur-basis definitions of \(I_{r,q}\), \(J_{p,c}\), and \(Q_{p,c}\), the requested target is established.
